blocks.md: Senior CP reflex: when values are huge but COUNT is small, throw away magnitudes and keep **ranks**. Almost every 'impossible' range problem becomes tractable after compression. The second reflex: when the STL lacks a query (rank? erase-middle?), GNU pb_ds probably ships it.
**Compress values to ranks → build on positions. If STL can't answer it, pb_ds can.**

chain.q: Why does deterministic unordered_map get hacked?
chain.a: Hacks precompute a family of keys where every key lands in one bucket (std::hash(ll) is identity on many libstdc++ builds). Your O(n) per op becomes O(n²). Fix: SplitMixHash with runtime seed — see Foundations L4.

chain.q: When is bitset the right container?
chain.a: Dense boolean universes ≤ ~10⁸ bits: sieve flags, subset-DP reachability ('can I form sum s?'), transitive-closure rounds (bitset-AND gives /64 speedup). Memory math must be stated in your head: bits/8 = bytes.

chain.q: deque vs vector in hot loops?
chain.a: deque's fixed slab indirection loses cache locality and has heavier iterators; default vector, reserve, and only switch for true both-end queues. In CP, deque often replaced by two vectors or ring buffer.
Exists on GCC 64-bit: holds products of two 10¹⁸ numbers (~10³⁶). No cin/cout — write print128 via digit extraction. Use ONLY as intermediate; final answers mod back to ll.

blocks.label: multiset running-median skeleton
blocks.py:
# two-heaps running median via heapq (lazy-free design):
import heapq
lo, hi = [], []                            # max-side negated, min-side
def add(num):
    heapq.heappush(lo, -num)
    heapq.heappush(hi, -heapq.heappop(lo))
    if len(hi) > len(lo):
        heapq.heappush(lo, -heapq.heappop(hi))

items.title: Inversion Count (PBDS route)
items.statement: Count inversions in n ≤ 5×10⁵ using ordered_set; then implement merge-sort version and compare constants.
hints: For each a[i]: inversions ending here = i − order_of_key(a[i]).

items.title: Running Median of Stream
items.statement: Median after each insert/delete, n ≤ 2×10⁵. Multiset-balanced solution; state invariant sizes exactly.
hints: Delete may come from either half — rebalance after EVERY op.
Alternative: two priority_queues + lazy deletion from Foundations.

items.title: Distinct Values in Range Queries
items.statement: Count DISTINCT values in [l,r], many queries. Offline sweep + BIT over last-occurrence positions.
hints: Keep BIT marking last position of each compressed value.
Answer = prefix sum at r minus prefix at l−1 of markers.

items.title: Anti-Hash Survival Test
items.statement: Frequency counting on up to 10⁶ values designed against identity hashes. Ship splitmix-seeded map; verify against a locally generated collision bomb.
hints: Seed from chrono clock — different every run.
Test BOTH default and custom maps on bomb input.
Fallback: sort+group runs O(n log n) unhackable.

items.title: K-th Order Statistic Online
items.statement: Interleaved insert/erase/query-kth on a dynamic set, n ≤ 2×10⁵ ops — nth_element unusable (no persistence); use PBDS.
hints: Compare against policy-tree-free alternative (sqrt decomposition) for understanding.

revisionCard: Compress values→ranks whenever structure size ≠ value range
pb_ds: order_of_key / find_by_order = rank machinery in O(log n)
Multiset-PBDS via stamped pairs; pairing_heap_tag + modify() = decrease-key
Deterministic hash gets hacked — seed SplitMix64 per run; sort+group is unhackable fallback
bitset = dense-boolean weapon: memory = bits/8; dp |= dp<<w word-parallelism
Two-multiset median: strict size invariant, rebalance every operation
Offline sweep pattern: sort queries by r, maintain BIT over latest occurrences

glossary.def: GNU policy-based data structures library — order-statistic trees, fat heaps.
Rank query (how many less?) or selection (k-th smallest?) answered in logarithmic time.
Relabel values by their rank in sorted-distinct order; shrinks index space to m.
Precomputed input forcing all keys into one hash bucket — kills naive maps.
Reads all queries before answering any; enables global sorting orders.
Distinct-range-count idiom: mark newest occurrence, prefix-sum counts uniqueness.
GCC 128-bit integer holding 10³⁶-scale intermediates; manual printing required.
